description:
should_gc's floor is young_bytes >= max(live_baseline, SIZE_TABLE[0]/2) = 512 B once live_baseline collapses; the major trigger's reference uses the same 512 B (next_generation). No measurement justifies it: inherited tip geometry (fz-gl6 d2ecc9d48, fz-sc8.184.3 888ec526f). Measured (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/notes.md round 2): trickle collects at 8,496 of 8,496 yields, each copying <256 B; a parent/child ping-pong collects at ~78% of 320k round trips and runs majors at tiny heaps. A near-empty collection costs ~35-40k instructions (msg ~71k). Floor 4/16/64 KiB: msg instructions -27%/-43%/-55%, enum/dist/maps mean RSS unchanged at 4-16 KiB; spin/trickle instructions only -0.4..-1.2%. Failed the pre-registered rule (2 of 3 near-empty workloads) because only msg gains. Next: an experiment across several message-passing workloads (fan-in, ring, request/reply with payloads) with the rule fixed first; derive the floor from what a collection costs vs the bytes it can reclaim rather than picking a constant.

Correction to the close reason: the 39% gift_copy / 18% collection split comes from a profile of a debug-runtime build of msg. It has not been re-measured on release. Explainer: https://claude.ai/artifact/EAx7onN67JBAT7LeRTr72X
title: A process with a nearly empty young generation does not collect at every park or yield
